# Vibration Damping Device

The vibration damping device is constructed with a tubular outer attachment member and an inner attachment member, which are connected to one another by a pair of main rubber portions spaced apart from each other along the axial direction. This configuration establishes the fundamental structural relationship between the two attachment members, providing the necessary support and flexibility for effective vibration isolation.

Situated between the pair of main rubber portions is a liquid chamber, which is divided by a partition portion. This partition portion serves a dual function: it couples the outer attachment member to the inner attachment member, while simultaneously separating the liquid chamber into two distinct sections along the axial direction. As a result, a first liquid chamber and a second liquid chamber are formed, positioned on opposite sides of the partition portion.

To facilitate fluid communication between these two chambers, the partition portion incorporates an annular rigid portion. This rigid portion contains a restricted passage—commonly referred to as an orifice—that connects the first liquid chamber to the second liquid chamber. As fluid flows through this restricted passage in response to vibrational input, the resulting flow resistance and resonance generate the desired damping effect.

In addition to the rigid portion, the partition portion features an annular elastic portion. This elastic portion is arranged adjacent to the rigid portion in the radial direction, allowing the two components to work in cooperation within the overall structure of the partition.

Notably, the elastic portion is compressed and deformed in the radial direction, causing it to make contact with the rigid portion in an unbonded state. Because the elastic portion is held against the rigid portion through compressive deformation rather than through a bonded connection, this arrangement simplifies manufacturing while ensuring a reliable sealing engagement between the two components. The unbonded contact also accommodates relative movement and helps maintain the integrity of the liquid chambers during operation.

# Vibration Damping Device

## Technical Field

The present invention relates to a vibration damping device that is suitable for use in supporting a vibration source, such as an engine or drivetrain component, in a manner that isolates and attenuates vibrations transmitted to a supporting structure such as a vehicle body.

## Background and Overview

In applications where a vibrating body must be resiliently supported relative to a stationary or comparatively stationary structure, fluid-filled vibration damping devices are commonly employed. These devices utilize the flow of an enclosed liquid between separate chambers to generate damping forces that counteract input vibrations. The present device provides an improved construction that achieves effective damping performance across a targeted frequency range while maintaining durability and ease of manufacture.

## Structural Configuration

The vibration damping device comprises a tubular outer attachment member and a tubular inner attachment member arranged in a coaxial or substantially concentric relationship. The outer attachment member is adapted to be secured to one of the vibrating body and the supporting structure, while the inner attachment member is adapted to be secured to the other. The two attachment members are elastically coupled to one another by way of main rubber portions.

These main rubber portions are disposed at positions that are spaced apart from one another in the axial direction of the device. By virtue of this axially-spaced arrangement, the main rubber portions cooperatively define, together with the outer and inner attachment members, an enclosed space that is filled with a working liquid. This enclosed space constitutes a liquid chamber capable of holding the damping fluid under sealed conditions.

## Partition Portion and Liquid Chambers

Positioned within the liquid chamber is a partition portion that divides the interior into two discrete regions, namely a first liquid chamber and a second liquid chamber. These two chambers are placed in restricted fluid communication with one another so that relative displacement between the inner and outer attachment members induces a pressure differential between the chambers, thereby driving the working liquid to flow from one chamber toward the other.

The partition portion is provided with an annular rigid portion. This annular rigid portion incorporates a restricted passage, commonly referred to as an orifice passage, through which the working liquid is caused to flow between the first liquid chamber and the second liquid chamber. The dimensions and length of the restricted passage are selected so as to tune the resonant flow characteristics of the liquid to a desired frequency, thereby producing effective damping at that frequency.

## Elastic Portion and Sealing Function

Adjacent to the annular rigid portion, the partition portion further includes an annular elastic portion. This annular elastic portion is disposed in a position neighboring the rigid portion and is formed of a resilient material such that it can undergo elastic deformation in response to applied loads.

A notable feature of the construction is that the annular elastic portion is subjected to radial compression, causing it to be elastically deformed such that it comes into contact against the annular rigid portion. Significantly, this contact is established in an unbonded state; that is, the elastic portion abuts and presses against the rigid portion without being adhesively fixed or vulcanization-bonded thereto. The radial compressive load ensures that the elastic portion is held in intimate, sealing contact with the rigid portion, thereby preventing undesired leakage of the working liquid past the partition and confining fluid communication between the chambers to the intended restricted passage.

## Operation and Advantages

In operation, when a vibrational load is input to the device, relative displacement occurs between the inner and outer attachment members, and the main rubber portions deform accordingly. This deformation produces a pressure difference between the first and second liquid chambers, which in turn forces the working liquid to flow through the restricted passage of the annular rigid portion. The controlled flow of liquid through this passage, together with the associated resonance and flow resistance effects, generates a damping force that effectively attenuates the input vibration.

By providing the annular elastic portion in radially compressed contact with the rigid portion in an unbonded state, the device achieves a reliable liquid-tight partition without the need for adhesive bonding processes at that interface. This arrangement simplifies manufacture, accommodates dimensional tolerances through the resilience of the elastic portion, and helps to maintain the integrity of the separation between the first and second liquid chambers over time. As a result, the device is capable of delivering effective and stable vibration damping performance through the controlled flow of liquid between the two chambers.

# Patent Abstract

## Vibration Damping Device

A vibration damping device comprising a first mounting member and a second mounting member coupled by an elastic body, wherein the elastic body at least partially defines a liquid chamber configured to be filled with a liquid. The liquid chamber is divided by a partition member into a first liquid chamber and a second liquid chamber, the first and second liquid chambers being in fluid communication through a restricting passage (orifice) that permits controlled flow of liquid therebetween.

The partition member includes a rigid annular portion and an elastic portion supported by the rigid annular portion. The rigid annular portion provides structural support and defines a mounting periphery, while the elastic portion is disposed to deform in response to liquid pressure fluctuations between the first and second liquid chambers. The elastic portion is configured to elastically displace when subjected to differential pressure, thereby absorbing high-frequency, low-amplitude vibrations, while the restricting passage attenuates low-frequency, high-amplitude vibrations through liquid column resonance.

The combination of the rigid annular portion and the elastic portion enables the device to effectively dampen vibrations across a broad frequency range, improving isolation performance and reducing the transmission of vibration and noise between the coupled members.

# Technical Summary: Vibration Isolator with Partitioned Damping Structure

## Overview

This vibration isolator employs a fluid-filled damping architecture featuring a partition assembly that divides two liquid-filled chambers. The partition structure is characterized by a hybrid construction combining a rigid orifice-defining component with an elastically deformable member maintained in a radially-compressed, unbonded contact configuration.

## Structural Components

### Partition Portion

The partition portion functions as the primary separator between the primary (pressure-receiving) liquid chamber and the secondary (equilibrium) liquid chamber. It comprises two principal elements:

**1. Annular Rigid Part**
- Constructed from a substantially inelastic material (e.g., metal or hard resin)
- Incorporates an **orifice passage** that establishes restricted fluid communication between the adjacent liquid chambers
- The orifice serves as the tuned flow path enabling liquid column resonance for vibration damping in a targeted frequency range
- Provides structural rigidity and dimensional stability to the partition assembly

**2. Radially-Compressed Elastic Part**
- Positioned adjacent to the annular rigid part
- Fabricated from a resilient elastomeric material (e.g., rubber)
- Installed in a state of **radial compression**, generating a preload contact force against the mating surface
- Maintained in an **unbonded (non-adhered) contacting state** with the adjacent rigid part

## Key Design Feature: Unbonded Contact Interface

The distinguishing characteristic of this isolator is the interface between the elastic and rigid parts:

- **No adhesive or vulcanized bonding** is present between the elastic part and the annular rigid part
- Sealing and retention are achieved solely through **mechanical radial compression**, which produces sufficient interfacial contact pressure to prevent liquid leakage between chambers
- The radial compression ensures the elastic part remains securely seated while accommodating dimensional tolerances

## Functional Advantages

| Feature | Benefit |
|---------|---------|
| Unbonded interface | Simplifies assembly; eliminates bonding process steps and associated costs |
| Radial compression | Ensures reliable fluid sealing without adhesive |
| Rigid orifice component | Provides stable, tuned damping characteristics |
| Adjacent elastic member | Permits controlled deformation and may contribute to secondary damping or membrane action |

## Operational Principle

Under applied vibratory load, pressure fluctuations in the primary chamber drive fluid flow through the orifice passage into the secondary chamber. The resulting liquid column resonance dissipates vibrational energy. The radially-compressed elastic part maintains chamber separation integrity while its unbonded mounting allows for straightforward manufacture and potential relative micro-movement under load without interfacial bond failure.

---

*Note: This summary describes a general structural configuration. Specific dimensional parameters, material specifications, and orifice tuning characteristics would be defined according to the intended application and target frequency response.*

# Fluid-Filled Vibration Damping Engine Mount

## Technical Field

The present invention relates to a fluid-filled vibration damping device suitable for use as an automotive engine mount, and more particularly to an engine mount having two axially spaced rubber portions and a liquid chamber divided into first and second fluid chambers.

## Summary of the Structure

An engine mount (10) constructed according to the present invention comprises a first mounting member (12) adapted for attachment to a power unit of a vehicle and a second mounting member (14) adapted for attachment to a vehicle body. The first mounting member (12) and the second mounting member (14) are spaced apart from one another along a central axis (16) and are elastically connected by a main rubber elastic body (18).

## Detailed Description

### Mounting Members and Rubber Portions

The first mounting member (12) comprises a generally cylindrical metal fitting having a threaded bore (20) for receiving a fastening bolt from the power unit side. The second mounting member (14) is formed as a tubular metal sleeve (22) disposed coaxially about the central axis (16) and radially outward of the first mounting member (12).

The main rubber elastic body (18) is divided into two axially spaced rubber portions, namely a **first rubber portion (24)** and a **second rubber portion (26)**. The first rubber portion (24) is disposed at an upper axial position adjacent the first mounting member (12), while the second rubber portion (26) is disposed at a lower axial position and is vulcanization-bonded to an inner circumferential surface (28) of the second mounting member (14).

An intermediate sleeve (30) is embedded between the first rubber portion (24) and the second rubber portion (26), such that the two rubber portions (24, 26) are axially spaced apart and connected in series along the central axis (16). This axial arrangement permits independent tuning of the spring characteristics of each rubber portion (24, 26).

### Liquid Chamber and Partitioning

A liquid chamber (32) is defined within the mount (10) and is filled with a non-compressible fluid (34), such as an ethylene glycol or water-based solution. The liquid chamber (32) is partitioned by a partition member (36) into a **first chamber (38)** and a **second chamber (40)**.

The first chamber (38) is a pressure-receiving chamber, one wall of which is partially defined by the first rubber portion (24), such that elastic deformation of the first rubber portion (24) directly induces pressure fluctuation of the fluid (34) within the first chamber (38).

The second chamber (40) is an equilibrium chamber, one wall of which is partially defined by a flexible diaphragm (42) formed of a thin, deformable rubber membrane. The flexible diaphragm (42) readily deforms to accommodate volumetric change of the fluid (34) within the second chamber (40) with substantially no resistance.

### Orifice Passage

The partition member (36) is provided with an orifice passage (44) placing the first chamber (38) and the second chamber (40) in fluid communication with one another. The orifice passage (44) is tuned to a predetermined frequency such that fluid (34) flowing through the orifice passage (44) exhibits a resonance action, thereby providing high damping with respect to low-frequency, large-amplitude vibration such as engine shake.

The partition member (36) may further include a movable rubber plate (46) supported within a housing recess (48) so as to permit small displacement, whereby high-frequency, small-amplitude vibration is absorbed to prevent an undesirable rise in dynamic spring constant.

## Operation

When vibrational load is input between the first mounting member (12) and the second mounting member (14) along the central axis (16), the first rubber portion (24) and the second rubber portion (26) undergo elastic deformation. Deformation of the first rubber portion (24) causes a relative pressure difference between the first chamber (38) and the second chamber (40), inducing a flow of fluid (34) through the orifice passage (44). The resulting fluid resonance provides effective vibration damping, while the axially spaced rubber portions (24, 26) cooperate to establish desired static and dynamic spring characteristics.
